argv:
Several customer reports about deleted comments, archived issues and search:

1. On an issue's page, the comment count still includes comments that were deleted. It must count only comments that have not been deleted (a reply counts like any other comment).
2. A deleted comment can still be found through search right after it was deleted. Deleting a comment must remove that comment, and only that comment, from search immediately: its replies and its issue stay searchable.
3. When an issue is archived, the issue disappears from search but its comments (and their replies) can still be found. Archiving an issue must also remove all of its comments from search, without touching the comments of any other issue or anything in another workspace.
4. Ops run the per-workspace search index rebuild after bulk imports or when the index drifts. After a rebuild, deleted comments, archived issues and the comments of archived issues are searchable again. The rebuild must index exactly the workspace's live content: its live projects, its non-archived issues, and the non-deleted comments on those issues (including a live reply whose parent comment was deleted) and nothing from other workspaces. Running it more than once must not create duplicate results.
5. A customer who bulk-imported a large backlog reports that after a rebuild their oldest issues still cannot be found, and on issues with very long discussions the earliest comments are missing. The rebuild must cover every live issue and every live comment, however many there are.
